classification.difficultyReason: Two trig calculations (cos and sin) from the diagonal, then add them for the fencing.

content.prompt: A rectangular paddock $ABCD$ has a diagonal track $AC$ of length 640 m that makes an angle of $37^{\circ}20'$ with side $AB$. Fencing is needed along $AB$ and $BC$. Find the total length of fencing, in metres correct to the nearest metre.

answer.worked:
The paddock is a rectangle, so triangle $ABC$ is right-angled at $B$ with hypotenuse $AC=640$.
$$\begin{align*}\cos37^{\circ}20'&=\frac{AB}{640}\\AB&=640\cos37^{\circ}20'\\\sin37^{\circ}20'&=\frac{BC}{640}\\BC&=640\sin37^{\circ}20'\end{align*}$$
The total length of fencing is the sum of the two sides.
$$\begin{align*}AB+BC&=640\cos37^{\circ}20'+640\sin37^{\circ}20'\\&\approx897\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
